records.title: The largest theft in history: North Korea likely behind the $6.4 billion Binance hack — update at 19:30 UTC
records.summary: Elliptic's 19:30 UTC update estimates $6.43B stolen and $2.84B frozen (its frozen-asset chart uses an approximately 12:55 UTC cutoff). It reports 233M XRP among assets still controlled by the attacker, 48M RLUSD sold before Ripple froze the remainder, approximately 823M USDC frozen by Circle, a $59.9M USDT Aave collateral position against 19,762 ETH debt described as near liquidation, and an AVAX→USDC→ETH route using Circle CCTP that produced 7,242.8 ETH. Elliptic assesses DPRK linkage as likely, not confirmed.
records.limitations: The exact XRPL receiver balance and ledger cutoff are not separately stated in the 19:30 update. Elliptic's DPRK attribution is an analytics-provider assessment; no government or law-enforcement confirmation is reported. CCTP use does not establish Circle knowledge or endorsement. The Aave collateral is USDT, not XRP.

records.title: Security Incident Update #2 (2026-10-30)
records.summary: Binance says approximately $6.3B in token assets were affected; it reserved more than $6.34B in company funds, with $5B held in exact impacted token assets (about 80%), and is buying the remaining 20% through market and OTC channels. It reports approximately $3B frozen on-chain, targets phased withdrawal restoration in approximately 34 hours subject to security checks, plans an initial PoR snapshot in 12 hours and results by Monday 2026-11-02, and expects a technical postmortem after verification.
records.limitations: Company-reported commitments and estimates are not an independent audit or proof of completed replenishment. The update does not disclose XRP-specific quantities, wallet coverage, execution prices or the split between market and OTC purchases.

records.title: The $6.3 Billion Binance Hack: 233 Million XRP Drained on the XRPL
records.summary: XRPLWin reconciles five successful Binance-labelled XRP payments totaling 233,461,943.1 XRP between 20:05 and 20:09 UTC on October 29. It reports a failed 42,750,000.1 RLUSD payment to the not-yet-activated destination at 20:04, five later failed XRP retries with tecUNFUNDED_PAYMENT (four repeated prior amounts and one attempt from an additional wallet rhWj9g…), and five 0.00001 XRP dust payments of unknown purpose. The article also reports a Check transaction at 22:35 UTC; that observation is later than this run's 22:03:36 UTC cutoff and is explicitly excluded from this snapshot.
records.limitations: The 22:35 UTC Check and the article's associated latest-balance statement are future-dated relative to this snapshot cutoff and are not admitted. The failed RLUSD and XRP transactions did not transfer the attempted amounts. The five successful payments are public-ledger events analyzed by a secondary provider, not independent off-chain custody evidence.

records.title: Binance Stolen $6.3 Billion: Analysis of the Attack Process and Stolen Fund Flows
records.summary: Beosin independently reports 233,461,943.1 XRP transferred from Binance-associated XRPL hot wallets to the same receiver and reports no subsequent XRP transfer in its observation. It separately traces multi-chain assets and freezes.
records.limitations: Beosin and XRPLWin analyze the same public XRPL transactions; their analysis is provider-independent but not a second underlying transaction source. The exact XRPL observation cutoff is not stated in the retrieved summary.

records.title: Freezing Tokens — native XRP is not freezeable by token issuers
records.summary: Official XRPL documentation states that issuers can freeze issued trust-line tokens, but this functionality does not apply to XRP because XRP is the ledger's native asset. XRP cannot be frozen by an issuer; issued tokens have individual, deep and global freeze controls.
records.limitations: Protocol-level inability to freeze native XRP does not prevent a custodial exchange, broker or other centralized service from restricting assets held in its own custody. This source does not establish the custody status of the attacker receiver.
